question: Select the correct option related to the function regulated by ovaries.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Menstrual cycle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** **Ovaries and the Menstrual Cycle:**

 
• Ovaries are female reproductive organs that play a central role in the menstrual cycle.
 
• They produce and release eggs (ova) during ovulation, a key event in the menstrual cycle.
 
• Ovaries secrete hormones, primarily estrogen and progesterone, which regulate the menstrual cycle.
 
• Estrogen is responsible for the development and maintenance of female secondary sexual characteristics.
 
• Progesterone prepares the uterus for implantation of a fertilized egg.
 
• The menstrual cycle involves the thickening and shedding of the uterine lining (endometrium).
 
• Estrogen stimulates the growth of the endometrium in the first half of the cycle.
 
• Progesterone maintains the thickened endometrium in the second half of the cycle.
 
• If fertilization does not occur, progesterone levels drop, leading to menstruation (shedding of the endometrium).
 
• The ovaries' hormonal output directly influences the duration and regularity of the menstrual cycle.
 
• Follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) and luteinizing hormone (LH) from the pituitary gland control ovarian function.
 
• Ovarian hormones, in turn, provide feedback to the pituitary gland, regulating FSH and LH secretion.
 
• The ovaries are the primary source of female sex hormones, which are essential for reproductive health.
 
• The menstrual cycle is a complex interplay of hormones and physiological changes.
 
• The ovaries are essential for female fertility.
 
• The ovarian hormones have impacts on bone density, and cardiovascular health.
 
• The ovaries contain follicles, which are sacs that contain the developing eggs.
 
• The process of ovulation is the release of a mature egg from a follicle.
 
• The corpus luteum, which forms after ovulation, secretes progesterone.
 
• The ovaries are vital for the proper functioning of the female reproductive system
